# Thyroid disorders

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Internal medicine > Endocrinology > Thyroid and parathyroid gland disorders > Thyroid disorders*

[Original Article Link](/library/5H0iIh)

---

## Summary

This article provides an overview of the most common <u>thyroid</u> disorders (<u>hypothyroidism</u> and <u>hyperthyroidism</u>) and <u>thyroid function testing</u>.




For more information on specific conditions, see the articles on “<u>Hypothyroidism</u>,” "<u>Hyperthyroidism and thyrotoxicosis</u>,” “<u>Thyroid nodules</u>,” and “<u>Thyroid cancer</u>.”

---

## Overview of thyroid-related disorders

| <br>Overview of clinical features in thyroid-related disorders <br> |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
|  | <u>Hypothyroidism</u> | <u>Hyperthyroidism</u> |
| Ocular | <br>* <u>Periorbital edema</u><br><br> | <br><br>* <u>Lid lag</u><br><br>* Lid <u>retraction</u> (“staring look”)<br><br>* <u>Graves ophthalmopathy</u> (<u>exophthalmos</u>, <u>periorbital edema</u>)<br><br><br> |
| Vocal | <br>* Hoarse voice, difficulty articulating words<br><br> | <br>* Tremulous voice<br><br> |
| Dermatological | <br><br>* Cold, dry <u>skin</u><br><br>* Decreased sweating<br><br>* Puffy appearance<br><br>* Pretibial <u>edema</u><br><br>* Coarse <u>hair</u><br><br>* <u>Hair</u> loss<br><br>* <u>Brittle nails</u><br><br><br> | <br><br>* Warm, moist <u>skin</u><br><br>* <u>Excessive sweating</u><br><br>* Infiltrative dermopathy, especially in the pretibial area (<u>pretibial myxedema</u>)<br><br>* Fine <u>hair</u><br><br>* Diffuse <u>hair</u> loss<br><br>* <u>Onycholysis</u><br><br><br> |
| <u>Thyroid</u> | <br><br>* <u>Goiter</u> (in <u>Hashimoto thyroiditis</u>)<br><br>* <u>Atrophic</u> <u>thyroid</u> (in <u>atrophic</u> thyroiditis)<br><br><br> | <br>* Diffuse, smooth, nontender <u>goiter</u>, often with audible <u>bruit</u> (in <u>Graves disease</u>)<br><br> |
| Metabolic | <br><br>* Cold intolerance<br><br>* Fatigue, decreased physical activity<br><br>* Weight gain (despite decreased appetite)<br><br><br> | <br><br>* Heat intolerance<br><br>* <u>Weakness</u>, fatigue<br><br>* Weight loss (despite increased appetite)<br><br><br> |
| Cardiovascular | <br><br>* <u>Bradycardia</u><br><br>* Myxedematous <u>heart</u> disease (<u>dilated cardiomyopathy</u>, <u>bradycardia</u>, <u>dyspnea</u>)<br><br>* Decreased <u>cardiac output</u><br><br><br> | <br><br>* <u>Tachycardia</u><br><br>* <u>Palpitations</u>, irregular <u>pulse</u><br><br>* <u>Hypertension</u> with widened <u>pulse pressure</u><br><br>* Increased systolic pressure<br><br>* Decreased <u>diastolic</u> pressure<br><br>* Abnormal <u>heart</u> rhythms (e.g., <u>atrial fibrillation</u>)<br><br>* <u>Chest pain</u><br><br><br> |
| Musculoskeletal | <br><br>* <u>Hypothyroid myopathy</u> (<u>proximal</u> <u>muscle weakness</u> with elevated <u>creatine kinase</u> levels)<br><br>* Entrapment syndromes (e.g., <u>carpal tunnel syndrome</u>)<br><br>* <u>Myoedema</u><br><br><br> | <br><br>* <u>Hyperthyroid myopathy</u> (<u>proximal</u> <u>muscle weakness</u> with normal <u>creatinine</u> <u>kinase</u> levels)<br><br>* Osteopathy (<u>osteoporosis</u>)<br><br><br> |
| Gastrointestinal | <br>* <u>Constipation</u><br><br> | <br>* Frequent bowel movements (due to intestinal hypermotility)<br><br> |
| Reproductive | <br><br>* Abnormal <u>menstrual cycle</u> (<u>secondary amenorrhea</u> or <u>menorrhagia</u>)<br><br>* <u>Galactorrhea</u><br><br>* Decreased libido, <u>erectile dysfunction</u>, <u>delayed ejaculation</u>, and <u>infertility</u> in men<br><br><br> | <br><br>* <u>♀</u>: oligo/<u>amenorrhoea</u>, anovulatory <u>infertility</u>, <u>dysfunctional uterine bleeding</u><br><br>* <u>♂</u>: <u>gynecomastia</u>, decreased libido, <u>infertility</u>, <u>erectile dysfunction</u><br><br><br> |
| Neuropsychiatric | <br><br>* Impaired <u>cognition</u> (concentration, <u>memory</u>)<br><br>* <u>Somnolence</u><br><br>* <u>Depression</u><br><br>* <u>Hyporeflexia</u><br><br>* <u>Woltman sign</u><br><br><br> | <br><br>* <u>Anxiety</u><br><br>* Restlessness<br><br>* <u>Insomnia</u><br><br>* Tremulousness (e.g., fine <u>tremor</u> in outstretched fingers)<br><br>* <u>Hyperreflexia</u><br><br><br> |





For further information, see “<u>Hypothyroidism</u>” and "<u>Hyperthyroidism and thyrotoxicosis</u>.”

## Thyroid function tests

| Overview of thyroid function tests in thyroid disorders |  |  |  |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ‎ |  | Etiology | <u>Thyroid function tests</u> |  |  |
| <u>TSH</u> level | Free T<sub>4</sub> | Free T<sub>3</sub> |  |  |  |
| <br><u>Overt hypothyroidism</u> | <u>Primary hypothyroidism</u> | <br><br>* <u>Hashimoto thyroiditis</u> (most common cause)<br><br>* <u>Iatrogenic</u> (e.g., following <u>thyroidectomy</u> or <u>radioiodine therapy</u>)<br><br>* Antithyroid medication (e.g., <u>amiodarone</u>, <u>lithium</u>)<br><br>* Transient <u>hypothyroidism</u> (e.g., <u>silent thyroiditis</u>, <u>subacute granulomatous thyroiditis</u>, <u>postpartum thyroiditis</u>)<br><br><br> | <br>* ↑<br><br> | <br>* ↓<br><br> |  |
| <u>Secondary hypothyroidism</u> | <br><br>* <u>Pituitary</u> disorders (e.g., <u>pituitary adenoma</u>)<br><br>* Infiltrative diseases<br><br>* <u>Iatrogenic</u> (e.g., following <u>pituitary</u> <u>surgery</u>)<br><br><br> | <br>* ↓<br><br> |  |  |  |
| Tertiary <u>hypothyroidism</u> | <br>* <u>Hypothalamic</u> disorders<br><br> |  |  |  |  |
| <u>Subclinical hypothyroidism</u> |  | <br><br>* Asymptomatic<br><br>* Same etiology as <u>primary hypothyroidism</u><br><br><br> | <br>* Mildly ↑<br><br> | <br>* Normal<br><br> |  |
| <u>Euthyroid sick syndrome</u> | <u>Low T<sub>3</sub> syndrome</u> | <br>* Occurs in severe illness or severe physical <u>stress</u> (most common in intensive care patients)<br><br> | <br>* Normal<br><br> | <br>* Normal<br><br> | <br>* ↓<br><br> |
| <u>Low T<sub>3</sub> low T<sub>4</sub> syndrome</u> | <br>* ↓<br><br> |  |  |  |  |
| Primary <u>hyperthyroidism</u> |  | <br><br>* <u>Graves disease</u><br><br>* <u>Toxic MNG</u><br><br>* <u>Toxic adenoma</u> (see “<u>Thyroid nodules</u>” and “<u>Thyroid cancer</u>”)<br><br>* <u>Postpartum thyroiditis</u><br><br>* <u>Subacute granulomatous thyroiditis</u> (<u>de Quervain thyroiditis</u>)<br><br><br> | <br>* ↓<br><br> | <br>* ↑<br><br> |  |
| Secondary <u>hyperthyroidism</u> |  | <br>* <u>Thyrotropic adenoma</u><br><br> | <br>* Normal/↑<br><br> |  |  |
| <u>Subclinical hyperthyroidism</u> |  | <br>* Same etiology as primary <u>hyperthyroidism</u><br><br> | <br>* ↓<br><br> | <br>* Normal<br><br> |  |





For further information, see “Diagnostics” in “<u>Hypothyroidism</u>” and “Overview” in "<u>Hyperthyroidism and thyrotoxicosis</u>.”
